citation.description: Ticket comment describes seven-arm experiment ruling out: quiet-host latency, pure process-creation delay, shared-repository contention alone, inherited PATH/Git variables. Root cause identified as scheduler/filesystem starvation on shared overloaded host (load p50 76.4 on 18-CPU machine, OSError: no resources to fork observed).

criteria.criterion: A discriminating experiment proves one root cause and rules out viable alternatives.

findings.criterion: Bug 'Repo-isolation HEAD watchdog false-fails under full-suite load' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
findings.detail: The investigation concluded this is an environment/config issue (shared-host oversubscription), not a product defect, and no code repair was made. The ticket explicitly states: 'A second 104-minute suite was deliberately not launched because it would exacerbate the saturation being investigated and one additional green run cannot reject a rare tail.' The observational full-suite run did not reproduce the five-second timeout, but the ticket acknowledges this cannot definitively prove the issue won't recur under the same overloaded conditions. The operational mitigation is to avoid overlapping suites — the underlying condition (shared-host oversubscription) can still cause the timeout to recur. The ticket remains in_progress with no code fix and no definitive proof the original scenario no longer reproduces.
findings.remediation: To satisfy this criterion, either: (1) demonstrate via a recorded full-suite run under the same overloaded conditions that the timeout no longer occurs (requires a code fix or environment change that prevents the oversubscription), or (2) close the bug with an explicit disposition that the defect is classified as environment-only and the criterion is waived, recording the specific evidence (run id, timestamp, outcome) in a ticket comment.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
